objection: Can you just send me some information?
hints: don't just agree and hang up
ask what they'd want to see
ask a question to keep the conversation going
offer a short, specific next step
model_answer: Happy to. So I send the right thing and not a 20-page brochure, what's the one thing you'd want it to answer? ...Honestly, it's usually faster if I walk you through it for 10 minutes. Does Thursday at 2 work?

objection: I'm not interested.
hints: make it easy to say no
model_answer: Totally fair, most people aren't when a stranger calls. Can I ask one quick question before I let you go, and if it's not relevant I'll hang up myself?

objection: Now's not a good time.
hints: give a quick reason to talk
model_answer: No problem, I caught you at a bad time. The reason I called is quick: it's about cutting your costs. What's better for you, tomorrow morning or Friday afternoon?

objection: We're happy with who we're using now.
hints: ask what they like about them
model_answer: That's great, I'd never want you to switch from someone who's doing a great job. What do you like most about them? ...And if you could change one thing, what would it be?

objection: It's too expensive.
hints: ask what they're comparing it to
tie price to value or cost of the problem
model_answer: I hear you. Too expensive compared to what? ...Let's look at what this problem is costing you now, because if it's more than the price, it's not really a cost, right?

objection: I need to talk to my partner first.
hints: ask what the partner will want to know
model_answer: That makes total sense, it's a decision you should make together. What do you think will be their biggest question? ...Why don't we set up 15 minutes with both of you so I can answer it directly? Would Tuesday evening work?

objection: Let me think about it.
hints: ask what specifically they want to think about
model_answer: Of course. Usually when someone says that, there's one part they're not sure about yet. Is it the price, the timing, or something else? ...Let's talk that through, and if it still doesn't feel right, no hard feelings.

objection: How did you get my number?
hints: get to the reason for the call
offer to take them off the list if they want
model_answer: Fair question. I found your company online, and I reach out to businesses like yours because we help with rising costs. If it's not relevant I'll take you off my list, no problem. Can I ask you one quick thing first?

objection: We already use a tool for that.
hints: ask what they like and don't like
model_answer: Nice, which one are you using? ...How's it working for you? If you could wave a magic wand and fix one thing about it, what would it be?

objection: Your competitor is half the price.
model_answer: They might be the right fit if price is the main thing. Can I ask what's driving the decision? ...Most teams that switch to us come from cheaper tools because of X. What would it cost you if that problem kept happening?

objection: We don't have budget this year.
hints: ask about the cost of the problem
explore ROI or funding from savings
model_answer: Understood. When does planning start for next year's budget? ...If this saves more than it costs, some teams fund it from the savings. Would it help to put numbers together you could show your team?

objection: We could just build this ourselves.
hints: ask about time and maintenance cost
talk about focus on core product
model_answer: Your team definitely could. The question is whether you want them to. How long do you think it would take to build and maintain? ...Most teams find it's months of engineering time that could go into the product your customers pay for.

objection: How do we know our data is safe with you?
hints: offer documentation or a security review
model_answer: Great question, and you should ask every vendor that. We're SOC 2 Type II certified and encrypt data at rest and in transit. What does your security review usually need? I can get our security team on a call with you.

objection: Switching tools would be too much work.
model_answer: Totally valid, nobody wants a messy migration. We handle the setup and data import for you, and most teams are running in two weeks. What if we started with one team as a pilot so there's no big risk?

objection: I don't really get what your product does.
model_answer: Fair, I should've been clearer. In plain English, we make sure your team never forgets to follow up with a customer. How do you keep track of follow-ups today?

objection: Call me back next quarter.
hints: find out if there's a real reason to wait
model_answer: Happy to. What happens next quarter that makes it a better time? ...If this problem is costing you now, waiting three months has a cost too. Can we at least put 20 minutes on the calendar for early next quarter so it doesn't slip?

objection: Why do I need an agent? I can look on Zillow.
hints: agree Zillow is great for browsing
model_answer: Zillow's great for finding houses. Where I come in is everything after that: writing a strong offer, negotiating, the inspection, and making sure nothing goes wrong in escrow. Have you made an offer before?

objection: Another agent said they'd list it for more.
model_answer: I get why that's tempting. I could tell you a higher number too, but the market decides the price. Here's what homes on your street actually sold for. Overpriced homes sit and end up selling for less. What matters more to you, the list price or the price you actually get?

objection: I'm not paying a six percent commission.
hints: data on FSBO vs agent sales
ask about their experience so far
model_answer: I totally understand wanting to keep that money. The real question is what you walk away with. Homes listed with agents here sell for more on average, often more than the commission. How has it been going with showings so far?

objection: We're going to wait until the market gets better.
hints: explain buying and selling in same market
ask about their timeline and goals
model_answer: That makes sense. What would 'better' look like for you? ...Keep in mind, if prices go up, the next house costs more too. What's driving the move in the first place?

objection: My last agent was useless. Why would you be different?
model_answer: I'm sorry, that's really frustrating, especially after months on the market. Can I ask what you felt went wrong? ...Here's specifically what I'd do differently: new price strategy, pro photos, and you'd hear from me every week.

objection: My cousin has a real estate license.
hints: focus on experience in the area
model_answer: That's great to have family in the business. Are they doing this full-time around here? Buying in this market takes someone who's writing offers every week, so it's worth making sure you get the best representation, whoever it is.

objection: Can you cut your commission to one percent?
hints: explain what the commission pays for
model_answer: I get it, it's a big number. That commission pays for marketing, photos, and me negotiating hard for your money. If I'd give my own fee away that easily, how hard do you think I'd negotiate with buyers for yours?

objection: I can sell it off-market to people I know.
model_answer: You might get it sold that way. The question is whether you'd get the best price with only a few buyers competing. What if we did a quiet launch to my investor list first, so you keep privacy but get competition?

objection: I already have insurance through work.
hints: explain it usually ends if you leave the job
model_answer: That's a great start. Do you know how much it is? Usually it's one or two times your salary, and it goes away if you change jobs. How long would your family need your income covered if something happened?

objection: I'm young and healthy, I don't need it.
hints: agree being young is an advantage
model_answer: Being young and healthy is exactly why it's cheap for you right now, and that price can be locked in for 30 years. Is anyone counting on your income, like a partner or a mortgage?

objection: I can't afford it right now.
hints: ask what would happen to kids
offer to find a price that fits
model_answer: I hear you, money's tight for a lot of families. Term life is usually less than people expect, sometimes a dollar a day. What would feel comfortable each month? Let's see what that buys to protect your kids.

objection: Life insurance is a scam. You pay forever and get nothing.
hints: explain it's protection like car insurance
model_answer: I get why it feels that way. It's like car insurance: you hope you never use it. The point is if something happens, your family isn't stuck. What have you heard that makes it feel like a scam?

objection: How do I know you're not a scammer?
hints: give license number or way to check
never ask for sensitive info early
model_answer: You should ask that, and I'm glad you did. My license number is on the state's website so you can look me up. I'll never ask for your bank info over the phone. Would you like your son or daughter to join when we talk?

objection: My wife and I need to discuss it.
model_answer: Absolutely, it's a family decision. What do you think her biggest question will be? Why don't we set 20 minutes with both of you so she can ask me directly? Would Sunday afternoon work?

objection: Why not buy term and invest the difference?
hints: agree it's often a good strategy
talk about specific needs like estate or business
model_answer: For a lot of people, that's exactly what I'd recommend. Where permanent coverage can make sense is estate planning or business needs. Can I ask what your goals are, and whether you have a business partner or estate concerns?

objection: I'll do it next year.
model_answer: What would be different next year? ...The tricky part is that prices go up every birthday, and if your health changes, you might not qualify. Let's at least get you a quote so you know where you stand.

objection: I'm just looking.
model_answer: Perfect, take your time, that's what I'm here for. Just so I can point you in the right direction, what's got you looking? Is your current car giving you trouble?

objection: The payment is too high.
model_answer: Okay, what payment would you feel good about? ...We have a few ways to get there, like a little more down, the base trim, or a different term. Which of those sounds best to you?

objection: My trade is worth way more than that.
hints: explain how you got the number
model_answer: I get it, nobody likes hearing a lower number for their car. Let me show you how we got there: the miles, the tailgate, and what similar trucks sold for at auction. Let's look at the whole deal and your payment, not just the trade.

objection: The dealer across town is cheaper.
model_answer: They might be. Is that for the exact same trim and color? ...We have yours on the lot today, plus free oil changes for two years. What matters most to you besides price?

objection: My dad said not to buy on the first visit.
model_answer: Your dad's giving you good advice. Honestly, I'd love for him to come see it too. Want to set up a time you both can come for a test drive?

objection: I don't want any add-ons.
model_answer: Totally fine, no add-ons. The only one I'd even mention is the maintenance plan, since you said you drive a lot for work. Want me to show you the math, or skip it?

objection: I'm waiting for my tax refund.
hints: ask why they need a car
model_answer: Makes sense. When are you expecting it? ...We could get everything ready now, credit approval, the car you want, so when the refund hits, you're in and out in an hour.

objection: Just send me your best number in writing.
model_answer: I'll get that to you. So it's actually useful, besides price, what matters most, uptime or service speed? Those change the total cost a lot. I'd love 20 minutes to walk you through it.

objection: Won't it damage my roof?
model_answer: Great question, it's the first thing I'd ask too. We inspect your roof first, and our installs come with a roof penetration warranty. How old is your roof, do you know?

objection: Did you not see the No Soliciting sign?
model_answer: You're right, I'm sorry about that. I'll be quick and if you want me gone, I'm gone. I'm only knocking because your neighbors' electric bills have jumped this year. Has yours gone up too?

objection: We might move in a few years.
model_answer: Totally fair. Homes with owned solar often sell faster, and the agreement can transfer to the buyer. How many years are you thinking?

objection: Our HOA won't allow solar panels.
hints: HOA can't ban, only reasonable requests
model_answer: A lot of people are told that. In California, the Solar Rights Act says HOAs can't ban solar, they can only make reasonable requests about placement. We handle the HOA paperwork for you. Want me to show you what it'd look like?

objection: My neighbor's bill went up after he got solar.
hints: explain how your deal is different
model_answer: I'm really sorry, and unfortunately that happens with some companies. Do you know what went wrong, was the system too small or was there a payment escalator? ...We size to your actual usage and guarantee production in writing.

objection: Your production numbers are inflated.
hints: invite them to check the math
model_answer: You'd be right to be skeptical, a lot of estimates are. Let's use your actual usage from your bill and the real sun data for your roof. And if we come up short, we pay the difference. Want to check the math with me?

objection: Solar is too expensive.
model_answer: It can seem that way. What's your electric bill running right now? ...With $0 down, a lot of people end up paying less per month than their current bill, so it's really just swapping one payment for a smaller one.

objection: Solar companies go bankrupt all the time.
model_answer: That's a real concern, some have. That's why the panels and inverters come with manufacturer warranties that don't depend on us. I can also show you our reviews and years in business. What have you heard?
